facts.text: I get pain in my lower jaw and under my jaw.
It started three months ago.
It only happens when I eat.

facts.item: jaw pain: what brings it on
facts.text: It's set off by the first bite of each meal.

facts.item: jaw pain: what makes it better
facts.text: It eases off as I keep eating, and it's gone within minutes after the meal.

facts.item: jaw pain: how long each episode lasts
facts.text: Each episode lasts less than two minutes.
It's a sudden, sharp, stabbing pain.
It's about 8 out of 10.
It's over my lower jaw and the glands under my jaw, worse on the right side.

facts.item: jaw pain: depends on the time of day
facts.text: It doesn't depend on the time of day.

facts.item: jaw pain: changes with body position
facts.text: My position makes no difference to it.
My voice hasn't been hoarse.
My face doesn't sweat when the pain comes.
My nose doesn't run with it.
It doesn't hurt to swallow.
I have no trouble swallowing.
I've never had surgery.
I haven't had any injury.
I don't have any medical conditions.
I don't take any medicines.
Nobody in my family has had symptoms like this.
I wear dentures.

findings.name: head and neck examination
findings.result: Dentures in place; no ulcers, deformities, masses, or lymphadenopathy.

findings.name: mouth and throat examination
findings.result: Pharynx, tonsils, soft palate and tongue normal on inspection and palpation.

findings.name: electrolytes and renal function
findings.result: Electrolytes and renal function within normal limits.

findings.name: CT from the skull base to the neck, with and without contrast
findings.result: No space-occupying lesions, masses, or other pathologic findings.

gold.reasoning: 1. Glossopharyngeal neuralgia was excluded—“Regional tenderness was absent, ruling out glossopharyngeal neuralgia.” 2. Laryngeal and hypopharyngeal disease and Frey syndrome were considered unlikely—“In the absence of hoarseness, dysphagia, and odynophagia, laryngeal and hypopharynx diseases and Frey syndrome were considered unlikely diagnoses.” 3. Salivary-gland tumors and other space-occupying lesions were excluded—“the CT scan…did not reveal any findings suggestive of head and neck space occupying lesion, mass…or any other pathologic findings.”

x001: s005 says only 'Vital signs were normal'; each standard parameter is given 'Normal'. Oxygen saturation is not given a record.

leakage.reason: The trigger is described as 'the first bite of each meal', the defining history in the source; it uses the words of the syndrome's name but does not name it.

source_issues: Episodes are said to last less than 2 minutes but also to resolve 'minutes after the meal' (s002); both are kept in the patient's words.
notes: Index visit: the outpatient presentation with three months of jaw and submandibular pain on eating (s001); all examination, laboratory and CT results belong to this evaluation.
The associated-symptom denials of s002 (hoarseness, facial sweating, runny nose, painful or difficult swallowing) are separate absent facts.
f019 is 'chronic medical problems' for 'no underlying disease'; f020 is the denial of medications.
